title: Dedicated Burst Capacity: PRD completion + stakeholder reviews + launch plan
creator: Lauren Bishop
content:
## Summary
Track PRD finalization and cross-functional approval for Dedicated Burst Capacity, plus the end-to-end launch plan (beta -> GA) including gating criteria, customer readiness, and comms.

This ticket is the “single pane of glass” for:
- PRD completeness (requirements, non-goals, SLOs, pricing assumptions)
- Review sign-offs (Platform, Infra/Fleet, Routing, SRE, Finance, Legal, CS/Sales)
- Launch milestones and readiness gates

## Context / Problem
Dedicated customers want predictable baseline capacity but have periodic peaks (batch jobs, indexing, launches, weekly spikes). Today the option is permanent scale-up (over-provision) or operational escalation for temporary capacity, both of which are slow and expensive.

We are introducing a controlled paid burst option: customers may temporarily exceed baseline by borrowing from Redwood-managed burst pools with strict guardrails to protect neighbor workloads and platform-wide SLOs.

## Goals
1) Paid burst option for Dedicated customers to increase throughput during predictable peaks without permanently resizing baseline.
2) Guardrails that protect non-burst tenants (no noisy-neighbor SLO regressions).
3) Observable + supportable behavior: clear denial reasons, dashboards, runbooks, and audit trail.
4) Packaging + billing integration: metering, caps, reporting, contract language.

## Non-goals (initial)
- Cross-region bursting (within-region only for v1)
- Customer-specific burst pools (shared managed pools only for v1)
- Spot-market / reservation trading mechanisms

## Primary artifacts
- PRD (Confluence): sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-burst-capacity-prd.json
- Design spec (Confluence): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/burst-pool-architecture-and-guardrails.json
- ADRs:
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-burst-pool-admission-control-semantics.json
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-fairness-model-for-shared-burst-pools.json
- Packaging proposal (Confluence): sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/dedicated-burst-option-packaging.json

## Requirements checklist (PRD “Done” definition)
### Product behavior
- [x] Define “burst” vs baseline usage (what counts as burst consumption)
- [x] Tenant-level config: enablement, per-tenant caps, max burst ratio, cooldown window
- [x] Denial semantics and client behavior (immediate deny vs queue/backpressure) with deterministic outcomes
- [x] Explicit guardrails: fairness, anti-starvation, fleet safety cap, global circuit breaker
- [x] Failure modes: telemetry lag, partial saturation, routing timeouts, safe fallback behavior

### Observability + supportability
- [x] Customer-visible reporting requirements (Console: usage, limits, denials)
- [x] Denial reason codes and support playbook expectations
- [x] SRE dashboards + alerts requirements, including neighbor impact indicators
- [x] Audit logging requirements for burst config changes and admin overrides

### Commercial requirements
- [x] Metering approach (what gets billed; idempotency / retries)
- [x] Packaging tiers / limits (what Sales can promise)
- [x] Contract language stubs (definitions, limits, exclusions, SLA expectations)

## Stakeholders / reviewers
Product: Lauren Bishop (owner), Chris Osei (Product Ops)
Platform Control Plane / Policy: Ethan Park, Jordan Lee
Fleet/Infra: Vanessa Ortiz, Keiko Yamamoto
Routing: Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon
SRE/Obs: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant
Finance/Legal: Rishi Malhotra, Laura Bennett, Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes
GTM/CS: Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer, Rachel Kim, Miguel Santos

## Milestones
### Discovery & design (2025-01 to 2025-02)
- [x] PRD drafted, reviewed, and approved
- [x] Pool model + guardrails design spec reviewed
- [x] ADRs approved (admission semantics + fairness model)
- [x] Pricing assumptions reviewed by Finance (pre-approval conditions captured)
- [x] Legal contract language draft reviewed (open issues tracked)

### Implementation (2025-03 to 2025-04)
Tracking via Engineering tickets / PRs (see dependencies). PM responsibilities:
- [x] Confirm v1 scope stays within non-goals (no cross-region burst)
- [x] Confirm denial reason codes align with Support expectations
- [x] Confirm Console requirements are scheduled (minimum viable customer view)

### Internal beta / dogfood (2025-05)
- [x] Beta customer selection criteria + success metrics (tracked in PM-541)
- [x] Readiness checklist for enabling burst for a tenant (CS + Support)
- [x] Game day plan reviewed and executed sign-off path defined

### GA rollout (target 2025-06)
- [x] Staged rollout approach: region/hardware allow-list + per-tenant enablement
- [x] Release gates: SLO regression-based auto-reduction/disable, global circuit breaker
- [x] Customer-facing documentation and enablement one-pager ready
- [x] Sales “what we can promise” statements approved

### Post-GA hardening (2025-07+)
- [ ] Tune fairness thresholds based on observed peak patterns and denials
- [ ] Improve prediction signals for pool sizing + reduce alert noise

## Launch gating criteria (must be green for GA)
1) Non-burst SLO protection:
   - No sustained p95 latency regression for non-burst tenants attributable to burst pools (as defined in SRE SLO doc).
2) Safety controls:
   - Global circuit breaker validated in game day.
   - Kill switch validated (per-region + global) + documented rollback procedure.
3) Metering correctness:
   - No double-counting on retries; reconciliation checks in place and validated with Finance.
4) Support readiness:
   - Denial reasons documented; Support playbook includes “what to do” and “what to tell customer”.
5) Security/compliance:
   - Audit events emitted for enable/disable, limit changes, and admin overrides; RBAC restrictions reviewed.

## Open questions (resolved)
- Queue vs immediate deny? -> Immediate deny with explicit reason codes; client guidance for retry/backoff; optional brief queueing only behind gateway backpressure (documented).
- Fairness model? -> Token bucket / WFQ hybrid with anti-starvation and priority tiers, with determinism guarantees under telemetry smoothing.
- What is billed? -> Burst-only consumption above baseline, metered with idempotency keys; billed as a distinct line item.

## Risks and mitigations
- Telemetry lag causes unfair denials or over-admission -> smoothing + guard conditions; “telemetry stale” denial reason; conservative fallback.
- Noisy neighbor tail amplification -> SLO gate to reduce/disable burst when neighbor impact detected; tuned circuit breaker thresholds.
- Confusion about expected 429/overload behavior at cap -> clear denial reasons + docs + CS onboarding checklist.
- Procurement constraints limit pool size in some regions -> staged rollout by region/hardware; safety buffers vary by supply risk.

## Notes
This ticket intentionally duplicates some “status” info from dependent Engineering work as a PM-level readiness view. Source of truth for implementation details remains ENG tickets and Confluence design spec.
comments: 2025-01-16 — Lauren Bishop: Draft PRD skeleton is up in Confluence. Key thing to align early: do we ever queue burst requests, or do we only deny + let customer retry/backoff? Adding to ADR discussion.

2025-01-24 — Ethan Park: Control plane schema proposal: per-tenant enable + burst_ratio_cap + absolute_cap + cooldown_seconds + priority_tier. Need to confirm validation rules and migration plan; will follow up in ENG-4816.

2025-02-03 — Vanessa Ortiz: Fleet perspective: burst pool sizing must be conservative in us-east H100 initially due to existing commitments. Recommend region/hardware allow-list for GA and hard global safety cap. Please capture as launch gate + rollback criteria.

2025-02-10 — Sean Gallagher: SRE stance: GA only with SLO regression gate wired (automatic reduction/disable) + game day executed. Add explicit neighbor-impact panels and paging policy update; otherwise we’ll be blind during bursts.

2025-02-21 — Laura Bennett: Finance approval conditional on (1) metering idempotency for retries, (2) reconciliation report available to CS/Finance within 24h, (3) pricing bands align with margin sensitivity model. Please ensure these are GA gates.

2025-03-07 — Michael Grant: Legal draft language in progress; request: product to be explicit that burst is best-effort capacity, with defined caps and explicit denial semantics; do not imply same latency SLA as baseline dedicated capacity.
2025-04-14 — Rachel Kim: CS needs a standard onboarding checklist and a single dashboard view we can share with customers. If Console UI slips, we need at least a shareable report export for beta/GA.

2025-05-09 — Talia Benson: Internal beta enabled for 3 internal tenants; early issue observed with telemetry lag causing denials to spike. Engineering working hotfix; adding as GA blocker until resolved and validated.

2025-05-27 — Allison Grant: Dashboards are in place; alert noise is higher than expected due to label cardinality on denial reasons. We’re constraining labels + updating alert grouping. Not a GA blocker but needs follow-up before broad rollout.

2025-06-05 — Lauren Bishop: Marking PM-512 Done. PRD + launch plan approved; GA rollout proceeding via region/hardware allow-list and per-tenant enablement. Remaining follow-ups tracked post-GA under separate tickets (tuning + alert noise reduction).
